Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE

Topic 2.1: Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of FAMILY CELEBRATIONS SUGGESTED VOCABULARY: celebrate, ribbon, ceremony, invitatio in Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should you pronounce sounds and words correctly? 2. Which words are used as subjects in a sentence?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. discriminate sounds and words for listening, comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. pronounce words containing target sounds accurately for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the importance of accurate pronunciation for effective communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to a variety of audio materials and identify sounds (/ɜː/ /ɑː/ /ɔɪ/ /aɪ/ / l/ /r/), words and expressions related to the theme,

2. listen to a passage or dialogue read by the teacher and identify the sounds /ɜː/ /ɑː/ /ɔɪ/ /aɪ/ / l/ /r/,

3. use vocabulary related to the theme to construct a variety of sentences,

4. team up to use word wheels with sounds /ɜː/ /ɑː/ /ɔɪ/ /aɪ/ / l/ /r/ to form new words such as load, road, boy, toy, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to a variety of audio materials and identify sounds (/ɜː/ /ɑː/ /ɔɪ/ /aɪ/ / l/ /r/), words and expressions related to the theme,
2. listen to a passage or dialogue read by the teacher and identify the sounds /ɜː/ /ɑː/ /ɔɪ/ /aɪ/ / l/ /r/,
3. use vocabulary related to the theme to construct a variety of sentences,
4. team up to use word wheels with sounds /ɜː/ /ɑː/ /ɔɪ/ /aɪ/ / l/ /r/ to form new words such as load, road, boy, toy, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner role-plays and creates a video collaboratively using

learnt sounds and words.

● Digital Literacy: The skills are developed as the learner watches a video and identifies words with target sounds.

Values:
● Unity: This is enhanced as the learner cooperates with peers to use word wheels to form new words with target sounds.

● Love: It is developed as the learner displays an attitude of care for others as they work together.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion: This is developed as the learner works together with peers harmoniously to complete tasks.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of pronunciation to their learning in Kiswahili.
